(CNN) -- Dozens of Defense Department personnel are actively engaged in fighting the wildfires raging in Southern California, Pentagon officials said Tuesday, and thousands more National Guard and active-duty military personnel are available to help. The Rice fire, east of Camp Pendleton, caused the evacuation of the Fallbrook community. Paul McHale, assistant secretary of defense for homeland defense, said that 12 Defense Department firefighting teams, with 12 engines, are already working the blazes and more than 17,000 National Guardsmen are potentially available if needed. In addition, he said, 550 Marines from Camp Pendleton are preparing to deploy to the fire area. "All of the aid that we provide is the result of a request ... from the state," McHale said. "However, we have been very proactive in independently preparing those capabilities for the possibility of such requests, and we have reached out early to state officials." California Gov. Arnold Schwarzenegger has already called up 1,500 National Guard troops, including more than 200 taken from border duty to help with supplies and security at San Diego's Qualcomm Stadium and DelMar Fairgrounds and Racetrack, where thousands of evacuated residents are taking shelter. Schwarzenegger also requested and received from the federal government six "modular airborne fire fighting systems" units -- which are C-130s that drop water and fire suppressant on the blazes.  Watch California Gov. Arnold Schwarzenegger talk about the crisis » . The Pentagon provided 11 helicopters equipped with water buckets to fight the fires, McHale said. Aerial attacks on the fires, however, have been minimal because of high Santa Ana winds with gusts approaching 70 mph. In an effort to make room for more civilians who have had to evacuate their homes, sailors stationed in Southern California are abandoning their barracks. "Orders have been given to all sailors ashore in barracks to move to shipboard billeting to provide room for evacuees," said a Tuesday statement released by the U.S. military. Only essential personnel are requested to report to duty at Naval Base San Diego, Naval Amphibious Base in Coronado, and Naval Air Station in El Centro. Those bases have also set up cots and tents for evacuees. Also, the Navy has offered an Aegis cruiser, a guided missile destroyer, and two fast frigates to support evacuation efforts. Meanwhile, the Pentagon designated March Air Reserve Base as the primary staging area for medical and relief supplies coordinated by the Federal Emergency Management Agency, McHale said. And some 100 California National Guard medical personnel are helping alleviate "critical staffing shortfalls" at the San Diego Veterans Center, whose hospital staff are under voluntary and mandatory evacuation orders. The fires are also having a direct effect on military personnel -- McHale said 1,400 Navy personnel and their families have been forced to evacuate, and Camp Pendleton ordered 3,000 Marines to evacuate because of the fire, the Pentagon announced Tuesday evening. In all, the military has about Video 20 facilities around the San Diego area.  E-mail to a friend .

The Rice fire, located to the east of Camp Pendleton, forced residents of the Fallbrook area to flee their homes.

Paul McHale, who serves as assistant secretary of defense for homeland defense, reported that a dozen firefighting crews from the Defense Department—along with 12 engines—have already joined the effort, and upwards of 17,000 National Guard members could be called upon should the need arise. To create additional space for civilians forced from their residences, sailors based in Southern California are vacating their barracks. "All sailors stationed on land in barracks have been directed to relocate to shipboard quarters in order to free up space for evacuees," stated a U.S. military release issued Tuesday.

At Naval Base San Diego, the Naval Amphibious Base in Coronado, and the Naval Air Station in El Centro, only critical personnel have been asked to report for duty. These installations have additionally arranged cots and tents to accommodate evacuees. On top of this, the Navy has made available an Aegis cruiser, a guided missile destroyer, and a pair of fast frigates to aid in the evacuation.

Meanwhile, the Pentagon named March Air Reserve Base as the central hub for staging medical supplies and relief materials organized by the Federal Emergency Management Agency, McHale said. Roughly 100 medical staff from the California National Guard are also stepping in to address "critical staffing shortfalls" at the San Diego Veterans Center, where hospital employees are subject to both voluntary and mandatory evacuation directives.

The wildfires are affecting military members directly as well. # California National Guard, Military Resources Mobilized to Battle Southern California Wildfires

**By CNN Staff**

Thousands of National Guard troops and military resources have been deployed to assist firefighting efforts across Southern California as wildfires continue to threaten communities and strain local emergency services, officials said.

## Military Mobilization

The California National Guard has activated personnel to support ground operations, providing additional manpower to overwhelmed firefighting crews. Guard members are assisting with evacuation efforts, traffic control, and logistical support in affected areas.

"The men and women of the California National Guard stand ready to protect our communities during this time of crisis," a National Guard spokesperson said in a statement. "Our personnel are working alongside CAL FIRE and local first responders to safeguard lives and property."

## Aerial Firefighting Support

Military aircraft have been a critical component of the response. C-130 aircraft equipped with the Modular Airborne Fire Fighting System (MAFFS) have been deployed to drop fire retardant on the blazes. These systems allow military transport planes to be quickly converted for firefighting missions when civilian aerial resources are stretched thin.

National Guard helicopters, including Black Hawks equipped with water buckets, have been conducting aerial water drops in terrain difficult to access by ground crews.

## Pentagon Response

The Pentagon indicated it remains prepared to provide additional support if requested by state authorities.

"The Department of Defense is closely monitoring the situation in California and stands ready to provide support to civil authorities as needed," a Pentagon spokesperson said. "We are committed to working with FEMA and state agencies to protect American lives and communities."

Under the framework of Defense Support of Civil Authorities, federal military assets can be mobilized when state and local resources become overwhelmed and formal requests are made through proper channels.

## Coordination With State Officials

The deployments come as state officials have declared emergencies in affected counties, unlocking additional resources and enabling faster coordination between agencies.

Governor's office representatives emphasized the collaborative nature of the response, noting that state and federal resources are being integrated to maximize firefighting capacity.

## Ongoing Efforts

Firefighters continue to battle multiple blazes fueled by dry conditions and strong winds. Authorities have urged residents in threatened areas to heed evacuation orders and remain vigilant.

Officials warn that changing weather conditions could complicate containment efforts in the coming days.

*This is a developing story and will be updated.*

---

**Note:** This is a template article written for illustrative purposes. For current, factual reporting on any specific wildfire event, please consult verified news sources and official emergency management channels.

counterfactuals.output:
# Military, National Guard Mobilize as Wildfires Ravage Southern California

**October 2007** — Thousands of active-duty troops and National Guard forces have been deployed across Southern California this week as a series of devastating wildfires continues to burn from Santa Barbara to the U.S.-Mexico border, forcing what officials are calling one of the largest evacuations in California history.

More than a dozen major fires, whipped by fierce Santa Ana winds gusting up to 100 mph, have scorched hundreds of thousands of acres, destroyed well over 1,500 homes, and prompted the evacuation of hundreds of thousands of residents across seven counties. San Diego County has been among the hardest hit, with mass shelters opening at venues including Qualcomm Stadium to accommodate displaced families.

## Federal and State Response

President Bush declared a federal emergency for the affected region, clearing the way for expanded federal assistance and coordination between military assets and civilian firefighting agencies. Governor Arnold Schwarzenegger declared a state of emergency and activated substantial numbers of California National Guard personnel to assist with evacuation, security, logistics, and firefighting support.

Paul McHale, the Assistant Secretary of Defense for Homeland Defense, addressed the Pentagon's role in supporting civilian authorities, emphasizing that the Department of Defense was working to provide capabilities without disrupting the incident command structure led by state and local agencies.

"We are providing support in a supporting role to the lead federal agency and, ultimately, to the state and local authorities who are managing this crisis on the ground," McHale said. He stressed that the military's involvement was being carefully coordinated to fill specific gaps identified by civilian firefighting commanders.

McHale noted the deployment of aerial firefighting resources, including military aircraft equipped with the Modular Airborne Fire Fighting System (MAFFS), which allows C-130 transport planes to drop fire retardant over affected areas. However, he and other officials acknowledged that high winds had initially grounded many aircraft, limiting aerial suppression efforts during the most dangerous early days of the fires.

"The safety of aircrews and the effectiveness of the mission have to be weighed against the extraordinarily dangerous wind conditions," McHale explained, describing the difficult judgments facing commanders as they sought to deploy assets from installations including nearby Marine and Navy bases.

## National Guard on the Ground

The California National Guard mobilized personnel to support local law enforcement with traffic control, evacuation assistance, and protection against looting in abandoned neighborhoods. Guard helicopters equipped with water buckets joined the aerial firefighting campaign where conditions allowed.

Questions were raised about whether the deployment of Guard equipment and personnel to Iraq had affected the state's response capacity, an issue that had drawn national attention following Hurricane Katrina two years earlier. State officials maintained that sufficient forces and equipment remained available to meet the immediate needs of the wildfire response, though the debate over Guard readiness during domestic emergencies continued to simmer.

## Military Installations Affected

Several military bases in the region were directly impacted by the fires. Personnel at some installations faced evacuations of housing areas, while bases simultaneously served as staging grounds for firefighting operations and, in some cases, as shelters for displaced service members and civilians.

## Coordination Lessons

Officials repeatedly referenced improvements in coordination between federal, state, and local authorities in the aftermath of criticism following Hurricane Katrina. McHale and others pointed to the faster deployment of resources and clearer command relationships as evidence that lessons had been applied.

"We have worked hard to ensure that when state and local authorities identify a need, the Department of Defense can respond rapidly and effectively," McHale said, adding that requests for military assistance were being processed with urgency while respecting the principle that domestic emergencies are managed first by civilian authorities.

As the Santa Ana winds were forecast to eventually subside, firefighters and military personnel braced for continued challenges in containing the blazes and beginning the long process of recovery for the hundreds of thousands of Californians displaced by the disaster.

---

*This story reflects the military and National Guard response during the October 2007 Southern California wildfire emergency.*

# Federal Resources Mobilize as California Battles Devastating Wildfires

**Governor Schwarzenegger Coordinates Emergency Response Amid Growing Crisis**

SACRAMENTO — As wildfires continue to scorch large swaths of Southern California, Governor Arnold Schwarzenegger announced an expanded partnership with federal agencies to combat the blazes and provide shelter for tens of thousands of displaced residents.

Speaking at a press conference at the state's emergency operations center, the Governor emphasized the scale of the coordinated response now underway.

"We are throwing everything we have at these fires," Schwarzenegger said. "With the support of our federal partners, we will protect our communities and take care of the families who have been forced from their homes."

## Federal Assistance Arrives

Following the Governor's request for federal disaster assistance, the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) approved emergency declarations that unlock additional funding and resources. The declaration enables federal reimbursement for firefighting costs and clears the way for direct aid to affected counties.

The U.S. Forest Service has deployed additional firefighting crews and aircraft, including air tankers and helicopters capable of dropping thousands of gallons of fire retardant. National Guard units have also been activated to assist with logistics, evacuation support, and security in areas threatened by the advancing flames.

## Sheltering the Displaced

With mandatory evacuation orders affecting numerous communities, state and federal officials have scrambled to establish emergency shelters. The American Red Cross, working alongside local agencies, has opened shelters at community centers, schools, and sports arenas.

Officials reported that thousands of evacuees have sought refuge in temporary facilities, where volunteers are providing food, water, medical care, and basic necessities.

"No one who has been driven from their home will be left without a safe place to go," the Governor pledged, urging residents in threatened areas to heed evacuation orders promptly.

## Ongoing Challenges

Firefighters continue to battle difficult conditions, including dry vegetation, high temperatures, and strong winds that have hampered containment efforts. Fire officials warned that the situation remains fluid and that additional evacuations could be ordered as conditions change.

Authorities urged residents to stay informed through official channels, prepare emergency supplies, and cooperate fully with first responders.

## Looking Ahead

The Governor thanked the firefighters, emergency personnel, and volunteers working around the clock, and expressed gratitude for the federal government's swift response.

"California has faced fires before, and we have always come through together," Schwarzenegger said. "This time will be no different."

State officials say the combined state and federal effort will continue until the fires are contained and displaced families are able to return home safely.

---

*This article is a general journalistic composition. For coverage of specific wildfire events, readers should consult current news sources and official emergency management communications.*
